utterances.text: The only purpose was to show that no one was ever punished for this crime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that -- I mean, you can still prove that point by what -- following the procedure suggested by Mr. Ackerman, with which I agree 100 per cent. I mean, you're not going to gain any ground by referring those documents to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I agree. If I may, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just put one question to the witness. Ask him whether he knows or he's ever heard of the name that appears on those documents or names. If he's in a position to tell us something about Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. them, then, yes, we go ahead and try to conclude. Because otherwise, Mr. Ackerman will not be having the 30 minutes that he asked for. Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I won't need the 30 minutes. I'm wondering if I could have the Court's permission for Mr. Jevtovic to consult with Mr. Brdjanin for a minute? There is something he wants to tell us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can go ahead, no? Yes, Madam Richterova, you can tender these documents --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to tender into evidence Prosecution Exhibit P739, which is regular combat report from the 6th December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is different. This is -- this is different. I mean, are we adding fresh documents now?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, this has already been tendered. I want to tender new Prosecution Exhibit P1620.1 until 6, because there are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Related?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, P1621 because 20 was the exhibit under seal. And this is a criminal file, so I want to tender it under one exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I only want to ask the witness one question with regard to the people who committed this crime.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Have you heard or did you receive an information of anyone who committed this crime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT31
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that a -- the men who perpetrated this crime was the soldier Mile and Zoran Simcic in Usorci, Mile Gvozden came to Tomasica to Nedjo Jovic's house and bragged that he was the killer. He said that he also -- that he killed seven people. One of them --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's apology.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT31
utterances.text: If anyone had survived, he said, the shooting, he would have slit their throat.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Witness, we had some difficulties at the beginning. You stated that it was Mile and Zoran Simcic and then later you stated, Mile Gvozden. So what were the names, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT31
utterances.text: Mile Gvozden and Zoran Simcic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: While you were in hospital or after you were released from hospital, were you ever contacted by an investigative judge or an investigator with regard to this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT31
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Were you ever called as a witness to the Prosecutor's Office in Banja Luka or to the Court in Banja Luka or to any other court with regard to this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT31
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And my last question: What are the consequences of the injuries which you sustained on the 5th of December?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT31
utterances.text: Well, the consequences are naturally I have problems with my right side of the jaw, and my arms. I have lots of difficulties, lots of problems with my illness -- and what else to tell you? I'll never be fully fit as long as I live.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I don't have further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Richterova. Sir, Mr. Ackerman, who is the lead counsel for the accused, will be putting some questions to you on cross-examination. Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I begin, I have a motion. Under the Statute of this Tribunal, Your Honours have limited jurisdiction, and only certain things are relevant to the issues before this Court. This is not something that you have jurisdiction over or that's relevant to any issue before this Court. This is just a common crime, no way has it been connected to the armed conflict that was going on in that area. The evidence before you now with these exhibits is that it was a couple of guys who were seeking revenge for the death of their brother and went off and committed a murder. That is not within the cognizance of this Court, and I therefore ask that you declare -- that you have no jurisdiction over this particular event and that it's irrelevant to any issue contained within this indictment. Because it's simply not a war crime. It's a crime, no question, that there was a horrible murder committed, horrible injury to this man. I feel nothing but extreme sympathy for him, but it was just a couple of criminal who is committed these acts and these acts are not war crimes. They are not cognizant to this Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Point taken, Mr. Ackerman, please file a proper motion so that it will give the Prosecution a proper opportunity to make submissions to the Court. And we will decide the appropriate moment on whether to keep this evidence in the record in order that it be taken consideration of in due course or whether to scrap it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Out of an abundance of caution, Your Honour, I will ask just some very brief cross-examination questions in the event that you decide to consider this evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It will happen rapidly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand that you are going to cross-examine him, without prejudice, in other words.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you almost no questions, very few, and the first thing I want to do is tell you that what happened to you is unforgivable and we are all very sympathetic with what you suffered. You've already told us that while you were hospitalised at the Paprikovac hospital in Banja Luka, that doctors there wanted to send you to Belgrade, and they wanted to do that because they didn't have the appropriate medication available to them in Belgrade, did they -- I mean Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT31
utterances.text: I suppose that was the reason that there were no conditions, there were no proper conditions there, they could not help me, and they wanted to send me to Belgrade. But why the doctor refused to sign it, that is something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. While you were there at that hospital, either in December, 1992 or January 1993, you were seen by a Muslim doctor, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT31
utterances.text: Yes. A Muslim doctor and a lady who was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Have you remembered the Muslim doctor's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT31
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Did you see other Muslim doctors working at that hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT31
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I want to ask you about some people. Dusko Kljajic his ethnicity -- Dusko Kljajic and Nevenka Knezovic were the two people who picked you up and took you to the ambulance, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT31
utterances.text: Correct. Dusko Kljajic is a Serb. Nevenka Knezevic is a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. And then you were visited in the hospital by Drago Jovic and Vucin Jovic, and what is their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT31
utterances.text: They are Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The doctor at Paprikovac who arranged for your release, you said in your statement that his first name was Ilija. Would that be the Muslim doctor that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT31
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. Sir, I hope you have a good trip home, and I hope the rest of your life is comfortable and enjoyable to you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT31
utterances.text: Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, sir, that brings us to the end of your testimony. I told you it would be a short testimony, that it won't last long. You are therefore now in a position to return back home after having been here in The Hague for quite some time. On behalf of the Tribunal, I thank you for having accepted to come over and give evidence, and may I assure you also that you will be given all the assistance by our staff to enable you to return back home safely. I wish you a safe journey back home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now -- yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please pull down the curtains.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I would ask that those persons in charge of finalising the transcript of this session compare what our transcript shows to what appears in the tapes, because the translations that we were getting were just not correct. It was almost every answer was not correct, and we didn't want to interrupt to change every answer. Mr. Brdjanin noticed it. Ms. Jevtovic noticed it. It just -- probably was an unfamiliarity with medical things, but it was not -- in many ways it wasn't even close. So it needs to be -- it really needs to be carefully reviewed it if we are going to have an accurate transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Ackerman. And I suppose that point has been taken up. Registrar, please, it's your task to coordinate this, up to the extent that it is necessary. Ms. Sutherland, as the senior one, or Ms. Richterova, I don't know who to address, do I take it that we are not starting with the next witness or are we starting with the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It looks that he was sent back so we will have to start with the new witness tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Please file the motion in writing, the motion that you have just raised, so that the Prosecution will have an opportunity to reply. If it needs be, then we give it a short hearing. On the other hand, please do refer to the records that we have here, the folder, to make sure that we won't waste our time. And another thing, Ms. Sutherland, I would appreciate if we had some sort of reply to Mr. Ackerman's motion for time off in February to enable --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a signed memo from Joanna Korner for Your Honours and a copy for Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You want to -- do you have any remarks, Mr. Ackerman, to Ms. Korner's memo?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yeah, only that I don't know that Dr. Stakic even has a family to come visit him so -- or what kind of arrangements there are made for that with him, but I can tell you that it is -- I mean, we have Status Conferences, frequently, to determine the conditions of detention, and that sort of thing. And one of the conditions that makes -- that's essential to I think, the mental health and well being of an accused is that he be able to see his family. So I think it's real harsh to say if Stakic hasn't seen his family no one else should without even knowing that he has a family to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll decide tomorrow. Thank you. The trial stands adjourned until tomorrow in the morning, 9.00.
